target_customer: B2B companies deploying AI agents in bounded, non safety-critical use cases (healthcare, finance, IT, legal, customer support and sales)
problem: Cyber and E&O policies exclude AI claims, so firms deploying agents have no coverage and no third party proof that their agents are safe for enterprise procurement.
business_model: Insurance and certification: risk evaluation, certification and AI agent liability coverage with premiums tied to an evaluation score
product_category: Liability insurance and certification for AI agents

founders.name: Ines Boutemadja
founders.background_notes: YC page: general manager at SafetyWing (W18) building carrier insurance infrastructure; per the launch post she structured a Tokio Marine MGA, obtained a Puerto Rico carrier license and helped scale an insurance startup from $5M to $60M revenue.

founders.name: Julien Catonnet
founders.background_notes: YC page: moved from corporate strategy consulting with corporates and insurers into software engineering at VC-backed startups; specific employers and education not listed.

competitors.name: Armilla AI
competitors.what: Standalone AI liability policy covering generative AI and agents, backed by Lloyd's capacity
competitors.traction_then: Underwrites using over 500 AI system evaluations (company claim)
competitors.funding_then: Cover limit expanded to $25M per organization, announced January 2025

competitors.name: AIUC
competitors.what: Certification first route (AIUC-1 standard) then insurance for AI agents
competitors.traction_then: News report says policies cover up to $50M in losses
competitors.funding_then: One comparison site reports a $15M seed; unverified

competitors.name: Testudo
competitors.what: Lloyd's backed third party AI liability insurance for enterprises deploying generative AI

technical_complexity.rationale: Behavioral testing with over 100 probes, governance scoring and a score to price pipeline is standard engineering, while the hard parts are underwriting data and carrier or Lloyd's capacity.

defensibility.rationale: Carrier relationships and underwriting data on agent failures accumulate over time, but established players like Armilla and AIUC were already selling.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not yet known; carriers were cautiously stepping into AI cover in early 2026 per press.

market_need_then: The company cites California AB 316 holding deployers liable, EU AI Act enforcement in August, and cyber and E&O policies excluding AI claims; trade press in 2025 and 2026 reported insurers struggling to price AI liability.

branding.domain_note: Uses klaimee.ai (.ai); USPTO word mark KLAIMEE application filed July 2025 in Class 45.

identity.visual_style: Clean light layout with dotted background visuals
identity.voice_and_tone: Direct and concrete, with plain examples and candor about limits

branding.brand_signature: The line 'You deploy agents, we cover you.'

brand_strength.rationale: A playful claim-based coinage that signals the product and a clear tagline, but no external press about the brand itself.

outcome_analysis: Klaimee is a Spring 2026 company that announced a $5.5M seed in July 2026 from Y Combinator, FundersClub and Robinhood Ventures. The CEO's SafetyWing background in building insurance products matches the need for carrier relationships, and regulation and policy exclusions create a tailwind. No exit or distress was found; the main risks are established AI insurers and capacity constraints.
notes: The $5.5M seed is stated on the company site and reported by fintech.global and Beinsure; the investor list comes from a Coverager summary seen in search and no lead investor was confirmed. Funding coverage is partial because no total or later rounds were checked beyond the seed. AIUC seed of $15M is unverified. Testudo launch date comes from an IUA document summary and a comparison site.
